newsitem.title: POLAND: ADTRANZ POLISH UNIT EYES NEW SALES.
newsitem.headline: ADTRANZ POLISH UNIT EYES NEW SALES.

text.p: Adtranz, whose recently acquired Polish plant has secured a major delivery contract for the State Railways, also wants the factory to sell rolling stock abroad and to the local market, Adtranz said on Tuesday.

Adtranz's deputy president Chris Sheppard confirmed that his company, which last month bought a 75 percent stake in rolling stock maker Pafawag SA for $3.7 million, planned to invest further $28 million in the company over the next six years.

"We want to invest in Pafawag $28 million over six years and establish company as a world class rolling stock supplier to Polish State Railways, Polish municipalities and for export market," Sheppard told a news conference.
Adtranz, a joint-venture of ABB group and Daimler-Benz, agreed to buy Pafawag under the condition that the firm would get a locomotive delivery order from the Polish State Railways (PKP).
The order, for 50 state-of-the-art locomotives, was placed last month, when a consortium of five Polish banks agreed to lend the PKP 633 million zlotys for the purchase.

Sheppard said on Tuesday the order covered 15 percent of Pafawag's production capacity and the company would soon seek new contracts, such as a delivery of underground wagons and tramways for the municipality of Warsaw.

Pafawag, based in the south western city of Wroclaw and employing 1,600 people, has reported losses for the last several years because it offered obsolete equipment and had no funds for modernisation, said Adtranz-Pafawag president Krzysztof Blaszczyk, also present.
He said the injection of capital, new technology and know-how from Adtranz was likely to prevent the company from cutting jobs.
